summary: Tag-driven project lifecycle automation: decommission Slack channels, snapshot Confluence spaces, archive Jira projects
description:
Issue summary:
We need a tag-driven project lifecycle automation that enforces a standardized decommission process for cross-team projects. When a project is marked with a lifecycle tag (e.g., lifecycle:decom-30d) in Jira or Confluence meta, the system should: 1) place the project's Slack channels into read-only mode and postfix the name with _archived-YYYYMMDD, 2) snapshot and store Confluence pages in a compliance S3 bucket (with metadata), 3) create an archival Jira project clone with reduced permissions and move open issues matching criteria, 4) notify project owners and start a 30-day quiesce countdown with opt-out, and 5) emit audit records to the compliance audit log.

Background / rationale:
We have several ad-hoc project shutdowns that are inconsistent: channels left open, docs drift, and missing audit trails. Legal/compliance requested a reproducible, auditable process for project offboarding that preserves data for eDiscovery and reduces clutter in Slack/Confluence/Jira. This automation should be permission-gated and require project-owner acknowledgement before irreversible archival steps.

Impact:
- Internal housekeeping: reduces stale channels and pages.
- Compliance: consistent snapshot and retention metadata for audits.
- Developer experience: avoids losing important artifacts while reducing noise.

Requirements / constraints:
- Non-destructive by default: first step is read-only / snapshot and notification; final destructive actions require explicit project-owner confirmation or 30-day expiry.
- RBAC: only Platform Admins and assigned project owners can opt-out or fast-track.
- Auditability: every action must produce an entry in the compliance audit stream (syslog/Kafka).
- Idempotency: automation should be safe to re-run and support retries.
- Rate-limits: operations must be rate-limited to avoid Slack API throttles.

Acceptance criteria (see separate field):

Related runbooks / references:
- Confluence design stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Tag-driven+Lifecycle+Automation+Design
- Slack channel archival best-practices: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Slack+Archival+Guidelines
acceptance_criteria: When a Jira project is tagged with lifecycle:decom-30d, an automated notification is sent to project owners within 1 hour.
Slack channels for the project become read-only and are renamed with _archived-YYYYMMDD but retain history within 2 hours of tag application.
Confluence pages are snapshotted to the compliance S3 bucket with metadata (project key, tag, timestamp, owner) and a checksum recorded in the audit log.
A cloned Jira project (read-only) is created and open issues matching 'critical' priority remain assigned; other issues are moved or closed per policy.
All automation steps emit audit events to /audit/lifecycle with sequence IDs and linkable metadata for eDiscovery.
Project owners can opt-out within the 30-day period via the acceptance flow; opt-out action is recorded in audit log.
Automation respects Slack rate-limits and retries transient failures without inconsistent partial state (idempotent runs).
comments: 2026-03-14 Jordan Kim: Filing request on behalf of Legal & Platform. Primary ask is reproducible audit trail + non-destructive default behavior. Attached initial design sketch in Confluence.

2026-03-14 Priya Desai: Thanks Jordan — a few clarifying Qs: (1) How should we determine project ownership for older projects without a defined owner? (2) Are we comfortable with cloning entire Jira project metadata or just exporting key issues? (3) Who signs off for final destructive steps?

2026-03-14 Jordan Kim: Proposed fallback owner policy: use last PR author within 365 days, then team lead mapping via HR group; if none, route to Platform Ops. For Jira cloning we prefer an initial 'issue export + read-only project' approach to avoid permission bleed. Final destructive steps require Legal + Platform Admin approval (two-person).

2026-03-15 Marcus Lee (Platform Eng): Quick note — Slack API renaming + setChannelReadOnly will be rate-limited; implement exponential backoff and a token bucket. Also recommend a dry-run mode for the first month targeting a single internal pod.
implementation_notes: Proposed approach: 1) Add a lifecycle tag recognizer lambda that subscribes to Jira/Confluence webhooks; 2) Enqueue tasks to a lifecycle worker (k8s) that runs sequential sub-tasks with compensating actions; 3) Use immutable snapshotting for Confluence (export HTML + attachments) to S3 and record checksum; 4) Use Jira project export to an archival project with restricted perms; 5) Use Slack SCIM / Admin APIs to set channel to read-only and rename; 6) Emit audit events to Kafka topic 'audit.lifecycle'. Start with a staged rollout for one internal team (pod: infra-ops) in staging region then prod rollout plan with feature flags.
resolution: Planned - design reviewed. Implementation sprint scheduled (Platform Eng sprint 2026-04). See Confluence design for gating and final sign-off checklist.
priority_notes: Not blocking customer traffic but high value for compliance and housekeeping; prioritize after current on-call rotations finish.
